title: Saudi-led coalition targets Red Sea territory held by Houthis. What's Pak's role?
content: Islamabad has not publicly acknowledged direct involvement in Saudi Arabia's offensive inside Yemen. However, several reports point that Pakistani forces could be helping Saudi Arabia shift more of its military resources towards the war by taking over defensive responsibilities inside the kingdom. That could allow Saudi forces to concentrate on the offensive against the Houthis without Pakistan formally becoming a combatant in Yemen.

title: Chirag Paswan's UP gamble: Why PM Modi's 'Hanuman' is flexing his muscle against allies

With plans to prepare for all 403 seats, the move could test the party's ability to build a Dalit vote base, influence close BJP-SP contests and strengthen its bargaining power within the NDA. His political journey from the 2020 Bihar split to a 19-seat win in 2025 provides the backdrop.

title: After warning AI may hurt everyone; Sam Altman says it should be broadly accessible
content: Sam Altman, the visionary CEO of OpenAI, asserts that the global community must embrace certain inherent risks tied to the evolution of AI technology. He posits that the benefits significantly overshadow the drawbacks, promoting the idea of AI being accessible to all. While he respects varied opinions from competitors like Anthropic regarding AI governance, he acknowledges the pressing demand for responsible oversight, a sentiment echoed by government authorities.

title: OFFSIDE: Why Sir Alex Ferguson vs Pep Guardiola is no longer a debate

title: Denzel Washington gave $1m to Texas debate team; it later won national title
content: Denzel Washington donated $1 million to Wiley College in Texas to revive its debate programme in 2007. The programme had been inactive since 1947 and soon regained prominence in collegiate debate. In 2014, the Wiley College debate team won a national tournament, defeating 80 other schools. Washington has since followed the team's progress and pledged to continue financial support.

title: Taylor Sheridan bought 600-acre Texas ranch; it later became film and TV hub
content: Taylor Sheridan's Bosque Ranch in Weatherford, Texas, has transformed into a prominent site for film and TV productions. Originally intended as a family residence, it now generates substantial income through shows like Yellowstone and 1883. The ranch doubles as an equine center, celebrating Western culture with competitions and housing over 150 horses, making it a hotspot for equestrian training. Sheridan's strategic expansions have added to his impressive property portfolio.

title: Marc Benioff, wife gave $100M to UCSF; 5 years later, children’s hospital opened

This hospital opened in February 2015, featuring advanced facilities designed exclusively for pediatric care. In addition, they made another $100 million donation in 2014 to further support pediatric research and clinical programs. The hospitals were renamed to honor the Benioffs for their generous contributions to children's health care.

title: Couple accidentally won 1830s house for $460,000; spent $300,000 restoring it

The couple decided to shift their approach to reuse materials and take on more work themselves. After about five years of work, the renovations are approximately 85% complete, although challenges remain.

title: Home to hotel: How short-term rentals are changing security in housing societies
content: Short-term rentals have raised security concerns in residential societies, as unknown guests frequently enter and exit. Incidents like a fatal fall in an Airbnb apartment highlight the potential dangers associated with transient occupants. Many housing societies are now issuing warnings against such rentals due to ongoing security issues. Legal challenges are emerging as residents seek to enforce restrictions on short-term accommodations.

title: Hyderabad tea stall owner walks into police station, sets himself ablaze

Parents should appreciate their children's quest for privacy while promoting open dialogue.

title: British Airways flight declares emergency after steep descent; lands safely in London
content:
British Airways flight BA295 declares emergency, descends to 9,000ft.

British Airways flight BA295 declared an emergency while flying over Ireland on Monday after the aircraft made a rapid descent from its cruising altitude. The Boeing 777 was travelling from London Heathrow to Chicago O'Hare when it descended from around 37,000 feet to approximately 9,000 feet while crossing Ireland. Flight-tracking data showed the aircraft's sudden change in altitude. The flight circled over the Bristol Channel after turning back towards the UK. The aircraft may be holding in the area to burn off fuel before landing, a procedure sometimes used when an aircraft needs to reduce its weight before making a precautionary landing. However, the flight landed back at London Heathrow after a reported pressurisation problem.
